blocks.path: Cellulitis
s: Cellulitis is a skin infection that's treated with antibiotics.
It can be serious if it's not treated quickly.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: your skin is painful, hot and swollen

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: Early treatment with antibiotics can stop cellulitis becoming more serious.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: You can call 111 or get help from 111 online.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Symptoms of cellulitis
s: Cellulitis makes your skin painful, hot and swollen.
The area usually looks red, but this may be less obvious on brown or black skin.
Your skin may also be blistered.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Symptoms of cellulitis
s: You may also feel unwell and have flu-like symptoms, with swollen, painful glands.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Symptoms of cellulitis
s: You can get cellulitis on any part of your body but it's more common on your lower limbs.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Treatment for cellulitis
s: For mild cellulitis affecting a small area of skin, a doctor will prescribe antibiotic tablets, usually for a week.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Treatment for cellulitis
s: Your symptoms might get worse in the first 48 hours of treatment, but should then start to improve.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Treatment for cellulitis
s: Contact your GP if you do not start to feel better 2 to 3 days after starting antibiotics.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Treatment for cellulitis
s: It's important to keep taking antibiotics until they're finished, even when you feel better.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Treatment for cellulitis
s: Most people make a full recovery after 7 to 10 days.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Treatment for cellulitis
s: If cellulitis is severe, you might be referred to hospital for treatment.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Treatment for cellulitis > To stop cellulitis coming back
s: Some people with recurring cellulitis might be prescribed low-dose long-term antibiotics to stop infections coming back.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Things you can do to help with cellulitis
s: As well as taking antibiotics for cellulitis, you can help speed up your recovery by:

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Things you can do to help with cellulitis
s: taking paracetamol or ibuprofen for the pain

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Things you can do to help with cellulitis
s: raising the affected body part on a pillow or chair when you're sitting or lying down, to reduce swelling

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Things you can do to help with cellulitis
s: regularly moving the joint near the affected body part, such as your wrist or ankle, to stop it getting stiff

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Things you can do to help with cellulitis
s: drinking plenty of fluids to avoid dehydration

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Things you can do to help with cellulitis
s: not wearing compression stockings until you're better

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Things you can do to help with cellulitis
s: You can reduce the chances of getting cellulitis again by:

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Things you can do to help with cellulitis
s: keeping skin clean and well moisturised

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Things you can do to help with cellulitis
s: cleaning any cuts or wounds and using antiseptic cream

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Things you can do to help with cellulitis
s: preventing cuts and scrapes by wearing appropriate clothing and footwear

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Things you can do to help with cellulitis
s: wearing gloves if working outside

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Complications of cellulitis
s: If cellulitis is not treated quickly, the infection can spread to other parts of the body, such as the blood, muscles and bones.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: You have cellulitis with:

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: a very high temperature, or you feel hot, cold or shivery

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: a fast heartbeat or fast breathing

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: purple patches on your skin, but this may be less obvious on brown or black skin

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: feeling dizzy or faint

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: confusion or disorientation

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: cold, clammy or pale skin

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: unresponsiveness or loss of consciousness

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: These are symptoms of serious complications, which can be life threatening.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: Do not drive to A&E. Ask someone to drive you or call 999 and ask for an ambulance.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: Bring any medicines you take with you.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > How you get cellulitis
s: Cellulitis is usually caused by a bacterial infection.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > How you get cellulitis
s: The bacteria can infect the deeper layers of your skin if it's broken, for example, because of an insect bite or cut, or if it's cracked and dry.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > How you get cellulitis
s: Sometimes the break in the skin is too small to notice.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > How you get cellulitis
s: You cannot catch cellulitis from another person, as it affects the deeper layers of the skin.

blocks.path: Cellulitis > How you get cellulitis
s: You're more at risk of cellulitis if you:

blocks.path: Cellulitis > How you get cellulitis
s: have poor circulation in your arms, legs, hands or feet, for example, because you're overweight

blocks.path: Cellulitis > How you get cellulitis
s: find it difficult to move around

blocks.path: Cellulitis > How you get cellulitis
s: have a weakened immune system, for example, because of chemotherapy treatment or diabetes

blocks.path: Cellulitis > How you get cellulitis
s: have lymphoedema, which causes fluid build-up under the skin

blocks.path: Cellulitis > How you get cellulitis
s: inject drugs

blocks.path: Cellulitis > How you get cellulitis
s: have a wound from surgery

blocks.path: Cellulitis > How you get cellulitis
s: have had cellulitis before

blocks.path: Cellulitis > How you get cellulitis
s: People who are more at risk of cellulitis should treat athlete's foot promptly.
